monthly_review.summary: This month shows a marked reduction in training volume and intensity compared to last month, with lower total km, fewer runs, slower average pace, and significantly less time spent in higher HR zones — indicating a deliberate or unintentional downshift toward recovery or base-building.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 3+ time dropped from 45% of total HR distribution last month (z3+z4+z5 = 26+15+4) to just 13% this month (z3+z4+z5 = 12+1+0), signaling a substantial shift away from threshold and VO2-max stimulus.

goal_tracker.message: You need 21.1 more km across 6 additional sessions (avg ~3.5 km/session) over the remaining 22 days to match last month’s volume — achievable with 2–3 short easy runs per week plus one longer run.

insights.title: Efficiency decline correlates with slower pace and reduced stride length
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency fell from 13.66 to 13.1 m/km per spm; notably, the May 6 long run (9.5 km) showed the lowest stride length (66.5 cm) and highest ground contact time (351 ms) — both likely contributors to reduced efficiency at endurance pace.

insights.title: Near-total absence of Zone 4–5 work this month
insights.body: This month’s HR zone distribution shows 0% in Z5 and only 1% in Z4 — down from 4% Z5 and 15% Z4 last month — suggesting loss of high-intensity stimulus critical for maintaining VO2 max and lactate buffering capacity.

insights.title: Cadence variability reflects inconsistent effort pacing
insights.body: Cadence ranged from 133 spm (May 2, 4.6 km @ 10:50/km) to 148 spm (Apr 28, 3.2 km @ 8:44/km); the slowest paces coincided with lowest cadence and shortest stride length — signs of form breakdown under fatigue or low neuromuscular engagement.

insights.title: Low HR and high Z1 time suggest intentional recovery focus
insights.body: This month’s 51% Z1 time (vs 23% last month) and avg HR of 130 bpm (vs 142 bpm) — especially on the May 5 run (121 bpm, 10:04/km) — indicate active recovery is occurring, which is appropriate if following a hard block but risks detraining if prolonged.

recommendations.action: Do a 5 km Zone 2 run at 132–138 bpm (per your recent avg HR range) with cadence ≥142 spm and stride length ≥75 cm — use May 2 as baseline for form cues.
recommendations.reason: Your May 2 run showed aerobic TE = 3.0 at 139 bpm and 133 spm — raising cadence while holding HR in Z2 will improve neuromuscular efficiency and stride consistency.

recommendations.action: Add one 8-minute Zone 3 interval session: 2 × 4 min @ 148–154 bpm with 3 min Z1 jog recovery — target avg pace ≤5:20/km based on your Apr 29 run (7:46/km @ 143 bpm).
recommendations.reason: You’ve done zero Z4–Z5 this month and only 12% Z3 — reintroducing threshold work will preserve VO2 max and lactate tolerance without overstressing recovery.

recommendations.action: Perform a 3 km easy run at ≤125 bpm with conscious focus on stride length ≥78 cm (use Apr 28 as reference: 77.4 cm @ 132 bpm) and vertical oscillation ≤7.5 cm.
recommendations.reason: Your longest run (May 6) had vertical oscillation of 7.1 cm but stride length dropped to 66.5 cm — reinforcing longer strides at low HR improves running economy and reduces ground contact time.

weekly_focus.description: Focus on re-establishing efficient neuromuscular coordination at Z2–Z3 intensities, bridging the gap between recovery and stimulus after a low-volume month.
suggested_sessions: Z2 rhythm run (5 km, 132–138 bpm, cadence ≥142 spm)
Z3 intervals (2×4 min @ 148–154 bpm w/3 min recovery)
Strides + form-focused easy run (3 km ≤125 bpm, stride length ≥78 cm)
